capabilities: Draw and write with pressure, pencil, and highlighter tools
Import PDFs and annotate them on notebook pages
Insert text boxes, sticky notes, LaTeX math, and wikilinks
Organize pages with thumbnails, bookmarks, and a grid overview
Export pages to PDF, PNG, or SVG
disambiguation: Not a PDF reader or annotation-only tool; it is a full handwriting notebook whose pages can also carry imported PDF backgrounds.
extras: Notebooks are stored as .gnote files (JSON schema with Obsidian frontmatter) and can be toggled to a Markdown/JSON source view. README covers stylus side-button behavior per platform, palm rejection, touch gestures, and performance for 100+ page notebooks. Feedback links point to a survey, GitHub Discussions, and the GitHub issue tracker.
motivation: The author wanted to combine pen-and-paper notebook feel with Obsidian's local-first, plain-text knowledge graph so handwritten pages stay inside the vault.
problem: Obsidian has no way to write freehand with a stylus or annotate PDFs, so handwritten notes and marked-up papers cannot live inside the vault.
summary: Local-first digital notebook and PDF annotator with stylus inking, paper templates, sticky notes, LaTeX math, and multi-format export.
